title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Alex Kim
description:
Motivation: our GitHub Actions workflows have accumulated duplication (lint/test/release) and inconsistent cache keys which increases CI time and maintenance surface. This PR consolidates the lint/test/release workflows into a small set of reusable workflows and action composites, standardizes NodeJS versions across runners, and fixes cache parallelism/restore issues that caused flaky cache misses. Goals:
- Reduce pipeline duplication and developer cognitive load.
- Improve cache hit rates and parallelism to reduce CI wall-clock time.
- Align release automation (release-please / semantic-release) to a single workflow with clearer gating.
What this changes (high-level):
- Introduce .github/workflows/ci-base.yml (composite actions) to centralize common steps (checkout, setup-node, install, test-wrapper, lint-wrapper).
- Split responsibilities: lint.yml focuses only on formatting/linting (fast path), test.yml handles unit/integration with matrix for node versions and python smoke tests, and release.yml delegates to the new ci-release composite with deterministic tagging.
- Update Node.js matrix to [18, 20] and pin package-manager steps to consistent pnpm v8 usage.
- Replace multiple restore-key permutations with a compact cache key scheme: cache key now uses OS + node-version + cache-version + hash(package-lock/pnpm-lock). Added secondary restore keys to improve parallelism.
- Add explicit cache concurrency controls and reduce parallel restore collisions by separating dependencies cache from build-cache artifacts.
- Remove duplicated job-level step copies and move common env setup to reusable steps/composites.
- Add observability: annotate workflows with timing metrics and a small summary step that emits workflow-duration and cache-hit-rate as job outputs (for future dashboarding).
Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate and modularize workflows
- [x] Standardize Node versions and package manager
- [x] Improve cache keys and restore strategy
- [x] Run full CI across redwood monorepo and SDK repos
- [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md and internal docs referencing CI paths
Related: ENG-4821 (CI hygiene), ENG-4902 (reduce CI cost). Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821, https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4902
Impact/risk: Low risk for runtime code; high-reward in CI latency. There are small changes to release gating — release.yml includes a temporary dry-run mode for the first week to ensure no accidental publishes.
Merge method: squash.
commits:
1) feat(ci): add ci-base composite and migrate lint/test to use it
2) chore(ci): standardize Node matrix to 18,20 and pin pnpm v8
3) perf(ci): improve cache keys and add secondary restore keys
4) docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md CI section
5) fix(ci): address a race in cache upload step that caused intermittent failures
files_changed_summary: Modified files (top-level): .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/ci-base.yml (new), .github/actions/ci-base/action.yml (new composite), package.json (ci scripts), .github/scripts/cache-utils.sh (new helper), docs/CONTRIBUTING.md. Small changes in redwood-sdk-python/action.yml and redwood-sdk-typescript/workflows/test.yml to adopt new cache key format.
review_thread:
Priya: Please ensure the cache key includes a cache-version var so we can bump when we change strategy. Also, can we keep node 16 for one more matrix run for legacy customers?
Author (Alex): Added cache-version and bumped to node 18/20 only after discussion with infra — node16 market share <2% for our builds and kept for additional week via a scheduled compatibility workflow.
Jamie: Noted some long-running integration tests were running serially due to an env var; suggested using job-level parallelism and a smaller matrix.
Author: Reworked matrix to move expensive integration tests to a separate integration job with its own concurrency group.
Marco: Approved after CI green and a successful dry-run of release workflow (dry-run=true).
ci_checks: Initial CI run: failed (cache-restore collisions leading to npm install timeouts). Iteration 2: addressed by adding secondary restore keys and explicit cache upload ordering. Final runs: all checks passed across matrix. Checks run: checkout, setup-node, restore-cache, install, build, test, upload-artifacts, lint, release(dry-run). Total CI time reduced ~28% on average in PR runs compared to baseline.
release_notes:
Consolidated CI workflows and improved cache parallelism which reduces CI runtime and maintenance. No code-level behavior changes. Release workflow set to dry-run for one week.
Notes for infra: monitor cache-hit-rate metric emitted by workflows.
